key_insight: Reinforcement learning can materially improve LLM-generated BPMN process models, but the reward-function design matters as much as using RL at all.
engineering_relevance: For structured generation systems, a simple equal-weight reward across quality dimensions can be more reliable than trying to manually target one metric, and model-specific training choices can strongly change outcomes.
method: Trained two LLM families: Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen 2.5 14B
Ran 48 RL configurations with Group Sequence Policy Optimization
Used an automated evaluation framework with 38 metrics spanning syntactic, pragmatic, and semantic quality
evidence_signal: The study evaluates outputs against 38 automated metrics across syntactic, pragmatic, and semantic dimensions, showing improved pragmatic and syntactic quality while preserving semantic fidelity.
watch_item: Reward shaping is highly architecture-dependent, so a configuration that works for one model may collapse performance or be unnecessary for another.
paper_title: Improving LLM-Generated Process Model Quality Through Reinforcement Learning: The Role of Reward Function Design
